sanskrit: tataḥ paripatan rājaṃs tasya kukṣau mahātmanaḥ himavantaṃ ca paśyāmi hemakūṭaṃ ca parvatam
english: Then, O king, flying within the belly of that great soul, I behold the Himavat and also the mountain Hemakūṭa.

sanskrit: niṣadhaṃ cāpi paśyāmi śvetaṃ ca rajatācitam paśyāmi ca mahīpāla parvataṃ gandhamādanam
english: I see the Niṣadha and also the Śveta mountain gleaming with silver, and, O lord of the earth, I see the mountain Gandhamādana.

sanskrit: mandaraṃ manujavyāghra nīlaṃ cāpi mahāgirim paśyāmi ca mahārāja meruṃ kanakaparvatam
english: O tiger among men, I see Mandara, and also the great mountain Nīla, and, O great king, I see Meru, the golden mountain.

sanskrit: mahendraṃ caiva paśyāmi vindhyaṃ ca girim uttamam malayaṃ cāpi paśyāmi pāriyātraṃ ca parvatam
english: I see Mahendra and the foremost of mountains the Vindhya, and I also see the Malaya and the mountain Pāriyātra.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo yāvantaḥ pṛthivīdharāḥ tasyodare mayā dṛṣṭāḥ sarvaratnavibhūṣitāḥ
english: These and many other mountains, however many uphold the earth — all of them were seen by me in his belly, adorned with every kind of jewel.

sanskrit: siṃhān vyāghrān varāhāṃś ca nāgāṃś ca manujādhipa pṛthivyāṃ yāni cānyāni sattvāni jagatīpate tāni sarvāṇy ahaṃ tatra paśyan paryacaraṃ tadā
english: O lord of men, O master of the world — lions, tigers, boars, and serpents, and whatever other creatures exist on the earth — all of these I beheld there as I roamed about at that time.

sanskrit: kukṣau tasya naravyāghra praviṣṭaḥ saṃcaran diśaḥ śakrādīṃś cāpi paśyāmi kṛtsnān devagaṇāṃs tathā
english: O tiger among men, having entered his belly and wandering through the directions, I also see Indra and the rest — indeed, all the hosts of gods in their entirety.

sanskrit: gandharvāpsaraso yakṣān ṛṣīṃś caiva mahīpate daityadānavasaṃghāṃś ca kāleyāṃś ca narādhipa siṃhikātanayāṃś cāpi ye cānye suraśatravaḥ
english: O lord of the earth, O master of men — gandharvas, apsarases, yakṣas, and sages as well; the hosts of Daityas and Dānavas, the Kāleyas, the sons of Siṃhikā, and whatever other enemies of the gods there are.

sanskrit: yac ca kiṃ cin mayā loke dṛṣṭaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam tad apaśyam ahaṃ sarvaṃ tasya kukṣau mahātmanaḥ phalāhāraḥ pravicaran kṛtsnaṃ jagad idaṃ tadā
english: Whatever I had seen in the world, moving or unmoving — all of that I now saw within the belly of that great soul, as I wandered about, feeding on fruits, traversing this entire world at that time.

sanskrit: antaḥ śarīre tasyāhaṃ varṣāṇām adhikaṃ śatam na ca paśyāmi tasyāham antaṃ dehasya kutra cit
english: Within his body I dwelt for more than a hundred years, yet nowhere could I find any end of his body.

sanskrit: satataṃ dhāvamānaś ca cintayāno viśāṃ pate āsādayāmi naivāntaṃ tasya rājan mahātmanaḥ
english: Constantly running and contemplating, O lord of peoples, O king, I could find no end at all of that great soul.

sanskrit: tatas tam eva śaraṇaṃ gato 'smi vidhivat tadā vareṇyaṃ varadaṃ devaṃ manasā karmaṇaiva ca
english: Then I sought refuge in him alone, that most worthy boon-giving god, with mind and deed, in the proper manner.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ sahasā rājan vāyuvegena niḥsṛtaḥ mahātmano mukhāt tasya vivṛtāt puruṣottama
english: Then suddenly, O king, O best of men, I was expelled with the speed of wind from the opened mouth of that great soul.

sanskrit: tatas tasyaiva śākhāyāṃ nyagrodhasya viśāṃ pate āste manujaśārdūla kṛtsnam ādāya vai jagat
english: Then, O lord of peoples, O tiger among men, he sat upon a branch of that very fig tree, having taken up the entire world.

sanskrit: tenaiva bālaveṣeṇa śrīvatsakṛtalakṣaṇam āsīnaṃ taṃ naravyāghra paśyāmy amitatejasam
english: O tiger among men, I see him seated there in that same form of a child, marked with the sign of Śrīvatsa, of immeasurable splendour.

sanskrit: tato mām abravīd vīra sa bālaḥ prahasann iva śrīvatsadhārī dyutimān pītavāsā mahādyutiḥ
english: Then, O hero, that child spoke to me, smiling as it were — the bearer of the Śrīvatsa mark, radiant, clad in yellow garments, of great brilliance.

sanskrit: apīdānīṃ śarīre 'smin māmake munisattama uṣitas tvaṃ suviśrānto mārkaṇḍeya bravīhi me
english: "O best of sages, O Mārkaṇḍeya, have you now dwelt within this body of mine and rested well? Tell me."

sanskrit: muhūrtād atha me dṛṣṭiḥ prādurbhūtā punar navā yayā nirmuktam ātmānam apaśyaṃ labdhacetasam
english: After a moment my sight returned anew, by which I saw myself freed and having regained my senses.

sanskrit: tasya tāmratalau tāta caraṇau supratiṣṭhitau sujātau mṛduraktābhir aṅgulībhir alaṃkṛtau
english: His two feet, dear one, with coppery soles, well-planted and beautifully formed, adorned with soft rosy toes —

sanskrit: prayatena mayā mūrdhnā gṛhītvā hy abhivanditau dṛṣṭvāparimitaṃ tasya prabhāvam amitaujasaḥ
english: — with my head, purified, I took hold of them and reverenced them, having seen the boundless power of that one of immeasurable might.

sanskrit: vinayenāñjaliṃ kṛtvā prayatnenopagamya ca dṛṣṭo mayā sa bhūtātmā devaḥ kamalalocanaḥ
english: Making a reverent gesture with joined palms and approaching with devotion, I gazed upon that god, the soul of all beings, lotus-eyed.

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ prāñjalir bhūtvā namaskṛtyedam abruvam jñātum icchāmi deva tvāṃ māyāṃ cemāṃ tavottamām
english: I, with joined palms, bowed to him and spoke thus: "O god, I wish to know you and this your supreme illusive power."

sanskrit: āsyenānupraviṣṭo 'haṃ śarīraṃ bhagavaṃs tava dṛṣṭavān akhilāṃl lokān samastāñ jaṭhare tava
english: "O blessed one, having entered through your mouth into your body, I have seen all the worlds in their entirety within your belly."

sanskrit: tava deva śarīrasthā devadānavarākṣasāḥ yakṣagandharvanāgāś ca jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam
english: "O god, within your body dwell gods, dānavas, and rākṣasas; yakṣas, gandharvas, and nāgas; and the world, both moving and unmoving."

sanskrit: tvatprasādāc ca me deva smṛtir na parihīyate drutam antaḥ śarīre te satataṃ paridhāvataḥ
english: "And by your grace, O god, my memory has not failed me, even while running swiftly and constantly within the interior of your body."

sanskrit: icchāmi puṇḍarīkākṣa jñātuṃ tvāham anindita iha bhūtvā śiśuḥ sākṣāt kiṃ bhavān avatiṣṭhate pītvā jagad idaṃ viśvam etad ākhyātum arhasi
english: "O lotus-eyed one, O blameless one, I wish to know you — having become a child here, why do you remain thus, having drunk in this entire universe? You ought to explain this to me."

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ ca jagat sarvaṃ śarīrasthaṃ tavānagha kiyantaṃ ca tvayā kālam iha stheyam ariṃdama
english: "And for what purpose, O sinless one, is the entire world lodged within your body? O subduer of foes, how long must you remain here?"

sanskrit: etad icchāmi deveśa śrotuṃ brāhmaṇakāmyayā tvattaḥ kamalapatrākṣa vistareṇa yathātatham mahad dhy etad acintyaṃ ca yad ahaṃ dṛṣṭavān prabho
english: "O lord of gods, O lotus-petal-eyed one, this I wish to hear from you, O lord, out of the desire of a brahmin — fully and truthfully — for what I have witnessed is great and inconceivable."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa mayā śrīmān devadevo mahādyutiḥ sāntvayan mām idaṃ vākyam uvāca vadatāṃ varaḥ
english: Thus addressed by me, that glorious god of gods, of great brilliance, the foremost of speakers, consoling me, spoke these words.

sanskrit: deva uvāca kāmaṃ devāpi māṃ vipra na vijānanti tattvataḥ tvatprītyā tu pravakṣyāmi yathedaṃ visṛjāmy aham
english: The god said: "O brahmin, even the gods do not truly know me in reality. But out of affection for you, I shall declare how I send forth this world."

sanskrit: pitṛbhakto 'si viprarṣe māṃ caiva śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ato dṛṣṭo 'smi te sākṣād brahmacaryaṃ ca te mahat
english: "O brahmin-seer, you are devoted to your ancestors and have taken refuge in me; therefore I have appeared to you directly, and your celibate discipline is great."

sanskrit: āpo nārā iti proktāḥ saṃjñānāma kṛtaṃ mayā tena nārāyaṇo 'smy ukto mama tad dhy ayanaṃ sadā
english: "The waters are called Nārā — a name I have given as designation; since that is always my resting place, I am called Nārāyaṇa."

sanskrit: ahaṃ nārāyaṇo nāma prabhavaḥ śāśvato 'vyayaḥ vidhātā sarvabhūtānāṃ saṃhartā ca dvijottama
english: "I am named Nārāyaṇa, the origin, eternal, imperishable, the ordainer of all beings, and also their destroyer, O best of twice-born."

sanskrit: ahaṃ viṣṇur ahaṃ brahmā śakraś cāhaṃ surādhipaḥ ahaṃ vaiśravaṇo rājā yamaḥ pretādhipas tathā
english: "I am Viṣṇu, I am Brahmā, and I am Śakra, lord of the gods; I am king Vaiśravaṇa, and Yama the lord of the departed."

sanskrit: ahaṃ śivaś ca somaś ca kaśyapaś ca prajāpatiḥ ahaṃ dhātā vidhātā ca yajñaś cāhaṃ dvijottama
english: "I am Śiva and Soma, and Kaśyapa the lord of creatures; I am Dhātā and Vidhātā, and I am sacrifice itself, O best of twice-born."

sanskrit: agnir āsyaṃ kṣitiḥ pādau candrādityau ca locane sadiśaṃ ca nabhaḥ kāyo vāyur manasi me sthitaḥ
english: "Fire is my mouth, the earth is my feet, the moon and sun are my two eyes, the sky together with its directions is my body, and wind abides in my mind."

sanskrit: mayā kratuśatair iṣṭaṃ bahubhiḥ svāptadakṣiṇaiḥ yajante vedaviduṣo māṃ devayajane sthitam
english: "By me have hundreds of sacrifices been performed with many well-bestowed fees; those who know the Vedas worship me, established in the sacrifice of the gods."

sanskrit: pṛthivyāṃ kṣatriyendrāś ca pārthivāḥ svargakāṅkṣiṇaḥ yajante māṃ tathā vaiśyāḥ svargalokajigīṣavaḥ
english: "On earth, lords of kṣatriyas and kings who desire heaven worship me; likewise vaiśyas who seek to win the heavenly world."

sanskrit: catuḥsamudraparyantāṃ merumandarabhūṣaṇām śeṣo bhūtvāham evaitāṃ dhārayāmi vasuṃdharām
english: "Having become Śeṣa the serpent, I alone uphold this earth, bounded by the four oceans and adorned by Meru and Mandara."

sanskrit: vārāhaṃ rūpam āsthāya mayeyaṃ jagatī purā majjamānā jale vipra vīryeṇāsīt samuddhṛtā
english: "Having assumed the boar form, this earth, which was sinking in the waters long ago, was lifted up by me through valour, O brahmin."

sanskrit: agniś ca vaḍavāvaktro bhūtvāhaṃ dvijasattama pibāmy apaḥ samāviddhās tāś caiva visṛjāmy aham
english: "O best of twice-born, having become the fire with the mare-mouth, I drink the waters that are stirred up, and then I release them again."

sanskrit: brahma vaktraṃ bhujau kṣatram ūrū me saṃśritā viśaḥ pādau śūdrā bhajante me vikrameṇa krameṇa ca
english: "The brahmin is my face, the kṣatriya my arms; the vaiśyas resort to my thighs; the śūdras worship me through my feet, step by step."

sanskrit: ṛgvedaḥ sāmavedaś ca yajurvedo 'py atharvaṇaḥ mattaḥ prādurbhavanty ete mām eva praviśanti ca
english: "The Ṛgveda, the Sāmaveda, and also the Yajurveda and the Atharvaṇa — these emerge from me and into me alone they return."

sanskrit: yatayaḥ śāntiparamā yatātmāno mumukṣavaḥ kāmakrodhadveṣamuktā niḥsaṅgā vītakalmaṣāḥ
english: "Ascetics whose highest aim is peace, those who restrain their souls and seek liberation, freed from desire, anger, and hatred, unattached, cleansed of impurity —"

sanskrit: sattvasthā nirahaṃkārā nityam adhyātmakovidāḥ mām eva satataṃ viprāś cintayanta upāsate
english: "— those brahmins who abide in the quality of sattva, free of ego, ever versed in the knowledge of the self, constantly contemplating me — they worship me."

sanskrit: ahaṃ saṃvartako jyotir ahaṃ sarvartako yamaḥ ahaṃ saṃvartakaḥ sūryo ahaṃ saṃvartako 'nilaḥ
english: "I am the fire of dissolution, I am the all-consuming Yama; I am the sun of dissolution, I am the wind of dissolution."

sanskrit: tārārūpāṇi dṛśyante yāny etāni nabhastale mama rūpāṇy athaitāni viddhi tvaṃ dvijasattama
english: "Those star-forms that are seen in the vault of the sky — know these to be forms of mine, O best of twice-born."

sanskrit: ratnākarāḥ samudrāś ca sarva eva caturdiśam vasanaṃ śayanaṃ caiva nilayaṃ caiva viddhi me
english: "The oceans, mines of gems, in all four directions — know these to be my garment, my bed, and my abode."

sanskrit: kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca harṣaṃ ca bhayaṃ mohaṃ tathaiva ca mamaiva viddhi rūpāṇi sarvāṇy etāni sattama
english: "Desire, anger, joy, fear, and delusion likewise — know all these to be forms of mine, O good one."

sanskrit: prāpnuvanti narā vipra yat kṛtvā karmaśobhanam satyaṃ dānaṃ tapaś cogram ahiṃsā caiva jantuṣu
english: "What men, O brahmin, attain through performing meritorious action — truth, charity, severe austerity, and non-violence toward creatures —"

sanskrit: madvidhānena vihitā mama dehavihāriṇaḥ mayābhibhūtavijñānā viceṣṭante na kāmataḥ
english: "— those ordained by my ordinance, who dwell in my body, whose understanding is overmastered by me, they act not of their own desire."

sanskrit: samyag vedam adhīyānā yajanto vividhair makhaiḥ śāntātmāno jitakrodhāḥ prāpnuvanti dvijātayaḥ
english: "Those twice-born who properly study the Veda, who sacrifice with various rites, whose souls are at peace, and who have conquered anger — they attain me."

sanskrit: prāptuṃ na śakyo yo vidvan narair duṣkṛtakarmabhiḥ lobhābhibhūtaiḥ kṛpaṇair anāryair akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: "Who, though knowing, cannot be attained by men of evil deeds, by those overcome by greed, by the wretched, the ignoble, the undisciplined of soul —"

sanskrit: taṃ māṃ mahāphalaṃ viddhi padaṃ sukṛtakarmaṇaḥ duṣprāpaṃ vipramūḍhānāṃ mārgaṃ yogair niṣevitam
english: "— know that I, of great fruit, am the refuge of those who perform good deeds, difficult to attain for those who are bewildered among brahmins, the path practised by those devoted to yoga."

sanskrit: yadā yadā ca dharmasya glānir bhavati sattama abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmy aham
english: "Whenever and wherever there is a decline of righteousness, O good one, and a rising up of unrighteousness — then I project myself forth."

sanskrit: daityā hiṃsānuraktāś ca avadhyāḥ surasattamaiḥ rākṣasāś cāpi loke 'smin yadotpatsyanti dāruṇāḥ
english: "When Daityas addicted to violence, invincible even by the best of gods, and dreadful rākṣasas are about to arise in this world —"

sanskrit: tadāhaṃ saṃprasūyāmi gṛheṣu śubhakarmaṇām praviṣṭo mānuṣaṃ dehaṃ sarvaṃ praśamayāmy aham
english: "— then I am born in the houses of those who perform auspicious deeds; entering a human body, I quell everything."

sanskrit: sṛṣṭvā devamanuṣyāṃś ca gandharvoragarākṣasān sthāvarāṇi ca bhūtāni saṃharāmy ātmamāyayā
english: "Having created gods and humans, gandharvas, serpents, and rākṣasas, and also the stationary beings, I withdraw them all by my own māyā."

sanskrit: karmakāle punar deham anucintya sṛjāmy aham praviṣṭo mānuṣaṃ dehaṃ maryādābandhakāraṇāt
english: "When the time for action comes again, I, meditating upon a body, create; entering a human body for the purpose of establishing the bounds of dharma."

sanskrit: śvetaḥ kṛtayuge varṇaḥ pītas tretāyuge mama rakto dvāparam āsādya kṛṣṇaḥ kaliyuge tathā
english: "White is my colour in the Kṛta age, yellow in the Tretā age; attaining the Dvāpara age it is red, and in the Kali age it is black."

sanskrit: trayo bhāgā hy adharmasya tasmin kāle bhavanty uta antakāle ca saṃprāpte kālo bhūtvātidāruṇaḥ trailokyaṃ nāśayāmy ekaḥ kṛtsnaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam
english: "Three parts of unrighteousness arise in that time; and when the time of the end arrives, having become an exceedingly terrible Time, I alone destroy the three worlds entirely, both the moving and the unmoving."

sanskrit: ahaṃ trivartmā sarvātmā sarvalokasukhāvahaḥ abhibhūḥ sarvago 'nanto hṛṣīkeśa urukramaḥ
english: "I am the one of three paths, the soul of all, the bringer of happiness to all worlds; the all-overcoming, all-pervading, infinite, Hṛṣīkeśa, the wide-striding one."

sanskrit: kālacakraṃ nayāmy eko brahmann aham arūpi vai śamanaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvalokakṛtodyamam
english: "I alone drive the wheel of time, O brahmin, truly formless — the pacifier of all beings, whose effort encompasses all worlds."

sanskrit: evaṃ praṇihitaḥ samyaṅ mayātmā munisattama sarvabhūteṣu viprendra na ca māṃ vetti kaś cana
english: "Thus is my self truly established, O best of sages, O lord of brahmins, in all beings — yet no one knows me."

sanskrit: yac ca kiṃ cit tvayā prāptaṃ mayi kleṣātmakaṃ dvija sukhodayāya tat sarvaṃ śreyase ca tavānagha
english: "And whatever suffering has befallen you, O brahmin — all of that in me leads to the arising of happiness and to your highest good, O sinless one."

sanskrit: yac ca kiṃ cit tvayā loke dṛṣṭaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam vihitaḥ sarvathaivāsau mamātmā munisattama
english: "And whatever you have seen in the world, moving or unmoving — in every respect that self is ordained to be mine, O best of sages."

sanskrit: ardhaṃ mama śarīrasya sarvalokapitāmahaḥ ahaṃ nārāyaṇo nāma śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ
english: "The grandfather of all worlds is half of my body; I am named Nārāyaṇa, the bearer of conch, discus, and mace."

sanskrit: yāvad yugānāṃ viprarṣe sahasraparivartanam tāvat svapimi viśvātmā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ
english: "For as long as a thousand cycles of yugas revolve, O brahmin-seer, so long do I sleep — I, the soul of the universe, the grandfather of all worlds."

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvam ahaṃ kālam ihāse munisattama aśiśuḥ śiśurūpeṇa yāvad brahmā na budhyate
english: "Thus I abide here through all time, O best of sages — not truly a child, yet in the form of a child — for as long as Brahmā does not awaken."

sanskrit: mayā ca vipra datto 'yaṃ varas te brahmarūpiṇā asakṛt parituṣṭena viprarṣigaṇapūjita
english: "And by me, O brahmin, in the form of Brahmā, this boon was granted to you — by me who am repeatedly gratified, O you who are honoured by the hosts of brahmin-seers."

sanskrit: sarvam ekārṇavaṃ dṛṣṭvā naṣṭaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam viklavo 'si mayā jñātas tatas te darśitaṃ jagat
english: "Having seen the entire world as one ocean, with the moving and unmoving vanished, you were bewildered — I knew this, and therefore I revealed the world to you."

sanskrit: abhyantaraṃ śarīrasya praviṣṭo 'si yadā mama dṛṣṭvā lokaṃ samastaṃ ca vismito nāvabudhyase
english: "When you entered the interior of my body and, having seen the entire world, were astonished and could not understand —"

sanskrit: tato 'si vaktrād viprarṣe drutaṃ niḥsārito mayā ākhyātas te mayā cātmā durjñeyo 'pi surāsuraiḥ
english: "— then, O brahmin-seer, you were quickly expelled by me from my mouth, and my self was declared to you — that which is difficult to know even by gods and asuras."

sanskrit: yāvat sa bhagavān brahmā na budhyati mahātapāḥ tāvat tvam iha viprarṣe viśrabdhaś cara vai sukham
english: "For as long as that blessed Brahmā of great austerity does not awaken, for so long, O brahmin-seer, roam here in confidence and happiness."

sanskrit: tato vibuddhe tasmiṃs tu sarvalokapitāmahe ekībhūto hi srakṣyāmi śarīrād dvijasattama
english: "Then when that grandfather of all worlds awakens, I, having become one, shall create again from my body, O best of twice-born."

sanskrit: ākāśaṃ pṛthivīṃ jyotir vāyuṃ salilam eva ca loke yac ca bhavec cheṣam iha sthāvarajaṅgamam
english: "Sky, earth, fire, wind, and water — and whatever else remains in the world here — the moving and the unmoving."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ity uktvāntarhitas tāta sa devaḥ paramādbhutaḥ prajāś cemāḥ prapaśyāmi vicitrā bahudhākṛtāḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having spoken thus, O dear one, that most wondrous god vanished, and I behold these creatures manifold and variously formed.

sanskrit: etad dṛṣṭaṃ mayā rājaṃs tasmin prāpte yugakṣaye āścaryaṃ bharataśreṣṭha sarvadharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: This was seen by me, O king, when that dissolution of the yuga arrived — this wonder, O foremost of the Bharatas, O best of all upholders of righteousness.

sanskrit: yaḥ sa devo mayā dṛṣṭaḥ purā padmanibhekṣaṇaḥ sa eṣa puruṣavyāghra saṃbandhī te janārdanaḥ
english: That god I saw long ago, with eyes like a lotus — that very one, O tiger among men, is your kinsman Janārdana.

sanskrit: asyaiva varadānād dhi smṛtir na prajahāti mām dīrgham āyuś ca kaunteya svacchandamaraṇaṃ tathā
english: By his very grant of a boon, O son of Kuntī, memory does not forsake me, and long life is mine, and also death at my own choosing.
